name: Goretek CompressLine Tactical Base Shirt
description:
A close-cut compression shirt in matte charcoal, constructed from four-way-stretch nylon-aramid blend with flat-lock seaming throughout. Reinforced shoulder panels are slightly thicker, designed to distribute pack straps and armor plate pressure. The collar sits high at the back of the neck with a discreet port-channel slit sized for standard neural port caps.

A staple in Circuit factories and transit yards. Holds its shape through twelve-hour shifts and repeated industrial washing. Faint reflective thread runs along the spine seam — barely visible, just enough for low-light safety compliance.
functionality: Compression supports muscle fatigue reduction across long shifts. Neural port channel slit accommodates standard-size BCI ports without collar pressure. Moisture-wicking inner face pulls sweat away from chrome-adjacent skin to prevent oxidation irritation. Machine washable to industrial cycle standards.
what_it_says: Practical, unbranded competence — someone who works hard and maintains their gear.
story_hooks: This specific batch was recalled by Goretek after reports of the aramid weave causing skin reactivity in users with dermal chrome — the recall notice never reached Tier 2 distribution.
The reflective spine thread doubles as a passive RFID strip in some production runs — workers are tracked without knowing.
A Circuit organizer uses the port channel slit to pass folded message strips between shift workers without raising floor camera flags.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, body-hugging compression shirt that reads as no-nonsense and utilitarian. The matte charcoal creates a near-shadow effect on the torso, broken only by a faint vertical reflective spine line visible in low light. High collar sits flush against the nape of the neck. Silhouette is athletic and streamlined—designed for function over fashion.
physical_description.fit: Compression fit—second-skin tight without restricting movement. Sleeves taper to wrist. Torso contours to the body. Reinforced shoulder panels create subtle bulk at the shoulder caps, suggesting the weight-bearing purpose of the garment.
physical_description.primary_material: Four-way-stretch nylon-aramid blend—industrial-grade synthetic with thermal regulation and durability properties. Matte finish minimizes shine.
physical_description.texture: Smooth to the touch with a slight brushed surface from the matte treatment. Seams are flat-locked throughout, creating no chafe points. Shoulder panels have a marginally thicker weave, almost imperceptible unless touched.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal gray (near-black) as primary. Reflective thread along spine seam is barely visible in daylight but registers as a faint silver line in shadows and night environments.
physical_description.closures: None—pull-over design with stretch-fit neckline. Port-channel slit at the high collar designed for neural augmentation caps (friction-sealed, no external fasteners).
distinctive_features: Reinforced shoulder panels for load distribution
Discreet rear-neck neural port-cap access port
Faint reflective safety thread running spine seam
Flat-lock seaming throughout for durability and comfort
Four-way-stretch construction for full range of motion
Matte finish for minimal reflectivity in tactical contexts
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—working-class industrial wear with quality construction. Not luxury, but built to last through heavy use.
physical_description.cultural_context: Circuit factory workers, transit yard staff, warehouse personnel, augmented laborers, courier crews. Signals someone doing hands-on work in the GLMZ's backbone industries. Also worn by lower-tier military contractors and private security as base layer under heavier gear.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in after a few washes—retains shape perfectly despite industrial laundering. May show minor wear at collar edges or subtle fading on shoulders from backpack/armor plate friction after months of use. Generally looks worn but intentional, never shabby.
